sanskrit: tasya kruddhaḥ sa nāgendro bṛhataḥ sādhuvāhinaḥ padā yugam adhiṣṭhāya jaghāna caturo hayān
english: Enraged, that lordly elephant of Uttara—huge and well-trained—set its foot upon the yoke and crushed all four of Śalya's horses.

sanskrit: sa hatāśve rathe tiṣṭhan madrādhipatir āyasīm uttarāntakarīṃ śaktiṃ cikṣepa bhujagopamām
english: Standing in his car whose horses were slain, the lord of the Madras hurled an iron spear, like a serpent, that would be the death of Uttara.

sanskrit: tayā bhinnatanutrāṇaḥ praviśya vipulaṃ tamaḥ sa papāta gajaskandhāt pramuktāṅkuśatomaraḥ
english: His armor pierced through by it, entering a vast darkness, he fell from the elephant's shoulder, his goad and lance slipping from his grasp.

sanskrit: samādāya ca śalyo 'sim avaplutya rathottamāt vāraṇendrasya vikramya cicchedātha mahākaram
english: Then Śalya, taking up his sword and leaping down from his splendid chariot, advanced boldly and severed the great trunk of the lordly elephant.

sanskrit: bhinnamarmā śaravrātaiś chinnahastaḥ sa vāraṇaḥ bhīmam ārtasvaraṃ kṛtvā papāta ca mamāra ca
english: Its vital parts torn by showers of shafts, its trunk cut off, that elephant gave a terrible cry of agony, then fell and died.

sanskrit: etad īdṛśakaṃ kṛtvā madrarājo mahārathaḥ āruroha rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ bhāsvaraṃ kṛtavarmaṇaḥ
english: Having performed this feat, the king of the Madras, that mighty car-warrior, swiftly mounted the gleaming chariot of Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: uttaraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā vairāṭir bhrātaraṃ śubham kṛtavarmaṇā ca sahitaṃ dṛṣṭvā śalyam avasthitam śaṅkhaḥ krodhāt prajajvāla haviṣā havyavāḍ iva
english: Seeing his noble brother Uttara slain, and seeing Śalya stationed there together with Kṛtavarman, Virāṭa's son Śaṅkha blazed up with wrath like fire fed with oblations.

sanskrit: sa visphārya mahac cāpaṃ kārtasvaravibhūṣitam abhyadhāvaj jighāṃsan vai śalyaṃ madrādhipaṃ balī
english: Twanging his great bow adorned with gold, the mighty one rushed forward, eager to slay Śalya, the lord of the Madras.

sanskrit: mahatā rathavaṃśena samantāt parivāritaḥ sṛjan bāṇamayaṃ varṣaṃ prāyāc chalyarathaṃ prati
english: Surrounded on every side by a great host of chariots, pouring forth a rain of arrows, he advanced toward Śalya's car.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya mattavāraṇavikramam tāvakānāṃ rathāḥ sapta samantāt paryavārayan madrarājaṃ parīpsanto mṛtyor daṃṣṭrāntaraṃ gatam
english: Seeing him bearing down with the might of a rutting elephant, seven of your warriors' chariots hemmed him in on all sides, seeking to rescue the king of the Madras, who had passed between the very fangs of death.

sanskrit: tato bhīṣmo mahābāhur vinadya jalado yathā tālamātraṃ dhanur gṛhya śaṅkham abhyadravad raṇe
english: Then the mighty-armed Bhīṣma, roaring like a thundercloud, seized a bow tall as a palm tree and charged upon Śaṅkha in the fray.

sanskrit: tam udyatam udīkṣyātha maheṣvāsaṃ mahābalam saṃtrastā pāṇḍavī senā vātavegahateva nauḥ
english: Beholding that mighty archer of vast strength rise up, the Pāṇḍava army trembled like a ship struck by the force of the wind.

sanskrit: tatrārjunaḥ saṃtvaritaḥ śaṅkhasyāsīt puraḥsaraḥ bhīṣmād rakṣyo 'yam adyeti tato yuddham avartata
english: Then Arjuna swiftly placed himself in front of Śaṅkha, thinking, "This man must be guarded today from Bhīṣma," and so the battle was joined.

sanskrit: hāhākāro mahān āsīd yodhānāṃ yudhi yudhyatām tejas tejasi saṃpṛktam ity evaṃ vismayaṃ yayuḥ
english: A great cry of dismay arose among the warriors fighting in the field; "Splendor has met splendor," they said, and were filled with wonder.

sanskrit: atha śalyo gadāpāṇir avatīrya mahārathāt śaṅkhasya caturo vāhān ahanad bharatarṣabha
english: Then Śalya, mace in hand, descending from his great chariot, slew the four steeds of Śaṅkha, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: sa hatāśvād rathāt tūrṇaṃ khaḍgam ādāya vidrutaḥ bībhatsoḥ syandanaṃ prāpya tataḥ śāntim avindata
english: Quickly taking up his sword, Śaṅkha fled from the car whose horses were slain, and reaching the chariot of Bībhatsu he found safety there.

sanskrit: tato bhīṣmarathāt tūrṇam utpatanti patatriṇaḥ yair antarikṣaṃ bhūmiś ca sarvataḥ samavastṛtam
english: Then from Bhīṣma's chariot the winged shafts flew swiftly forth, and by them the sky and the earth were everywhere overspread.

sanskrit: pāñcālān atha matsyāṃś ca kekayāṃś ca prabhadrakān bhīṣmaḥ praharatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ pātayām āsa mārgaṇaiḥ
english: The Pāñcālas, the Matsyas, the Kekayas, and the Prabhadrakas—Bhīṣma, the foremost of strikers, laid them low with his arrows.

sanskrit: utsṛjya samare tūrṇaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ savyasācinam abhyadravata pāñcālyaṃ drupadaṃ senayā vṛtam priyaṃ saṃbandhinaṃ rājañ śarān avakiran bahūn
english: Quickly leaving the Pāṇḍava Savyasācin on the field, he rushed against the Pāñcāla Drupada, who was surrounded by his army; and upon that dear kinsman, O king, he poured down a multitude of shafts.

sanskrit: agnineva pradagdhāni vanāni śiśirātyaye śaradagdhāny adṛśyanta sainyāni drupadasya ha atiṣṭhata raṇe bhīṣmo vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ
english: Like forests scorched by fire at winter's end, the troops of Drupada appeared, burnt up by his arrows; and Bhīṣma stood in the battle like a smokeless flame.

sanskrit: madhyaṃdine yathādityaṃ tapantam iva tejasā na śekuḥ pāṇḍaveyasya yodhā bhīṣmaṃ nirīkṣitum
english: As none can gaze upon the midday sun blazing with its splendor, so the warriors of the Pāṇḍava could not look upon Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: vīkṣāṃ cakruḥ samantāt te pāṇḍavā bhayapīḍitāḥ trātāraṃ nādhyagacchanta gāvaḥ śītārditā iva
english: The Pāṇḍavas, oppressed by fear, looked about them on every side, but found no protector, like cattle tormented by the cold.

sanskrit: hatavipradrute sainye nirutsāhe vimardite hāhākāro mahān āsīt pāṇḍusainyeṣu bhārata
english: As the army, struck down and scattered, dispirited and crushed, gave way, a great cry of distress arose among the troops of the Pāṇḍus, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo nityaṃ maṇḍalakārmukaḥ mumoca bāṇān dīptāgrān ahīn āśīviṣān iva
english: Then Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, his bow ever drawn into a circle, loosed flaming-tipped shafts like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: śarair ekāyanīkurvan diśaḥ sarvā yatavrataḥ jaghāna pāṇḍavarathān ādiśyādiśya bhārata
english: Making all the quarters a single path with his arrows, that man of firm vows slew the chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, singling out each one by name, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ sainyeṣu bhagneṣu mathiteṣu ca sarvaśaḥ prāpte cāstaṃ dinakare na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: Then, as the armies broke and were churned to pieces on every side, and as the maker of day reached his setting, nothing whatever could be discerned.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaṃ ca samudīryantaṃ dṛṣṭvā pārthā mahāhave avahāram akurvanta sainyānāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: And seeing Bhīṣma raging on in that great battle, the sons of Pṛthā sounded the recall of their troops, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca kṛte 'vahāre sainyānāṃ prathame bharatarṣabha bhīṣme ca yudhi saṃrabdhe hṛṣṭe duryodhane tathā
english: Saṃjaya said: When the first day's withdrawal of the armies had been made, O bull of the Bharatas—Bhīṣma furious in the fight and Duryodhana exultant—

sanskrit: dharmarājas tatas tūrṇam abhigamya janārdanam bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ sarvaiḥ sarvaiś caiva janeśvaraiḥ
english: the Dharma-king, going swiftly to Janārdana, together with all his brothers and all the lords of men,

sanskrit: śucā paramayā yuktaś cintayānaḥ parājayam vārṣṇeyam abravīd rājan dṛṣṭvā bhīṣmasya vikramam
english: filled with the deepest grief, brooding upon defeat, spoke thus to the scion of the Vṛṣṇis, O king, having beheld Bhīṣma's prowess:

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa paśya maheṣvāsaṃ bhīṣmaṃ bhīmaparākramam śarair dahantaṃ sainyaṃ me grīṣme kakṣam ivānalam
english: "Kṛṣṇa, behold the great archer Bhīṣma of terrible might, burning up my army with his shafts as fire burns dry grass in summer.

sanskrit: katham enaṃ mahātmānaṃ śakṣyāmaḥ prativīkṣitum lelihyamānaṃ sainyaṃ me haviṣmantam ivānalam
english: How shall we even be able to look upon this great soul, who licks up my army as fire licks at the oblation?

sanskrit: etaṃ hi puruṣavyāghraṃ dhanuṣmantaṃ mahābalam dṛṣṭvā vipradrutaṃ sainyaṃ madīyaṃ mārgaṇāhatam
english: For at the sight of this tiger among men, this mighty bowman of vast strength, my army has scattered in flight, smitten by his arrows.

sanskrit: śakyo jetuṃ yamaḥ kruddho vajrapāṇiś ca saṃyuge varuṇaḥ pāśabhṛc cāpi kubero vā gadādharaḥ
english: Yama in his wrath might be conquered in battle, and the wielder of the thunderbolt, and Varuṇa bearing his noose, and Kubera with his mace—

sanskrit: na tu bhīṣmo mahātejāḥ śakyo jetuṃ mahābalaḥ so 'ham evaṃ gate magno bhīṣmāgādhajale 'plavaḥ
english: but Bhīṣma of vast splendor and mighty strength cannot be conquered. So matters standing, I am sunk in the fathomless waters of Bhīṣma, without a raft.

sanskrit: ātmano buddhidaurbalyād bhīṣmam āsādya keśava vanaṃ yāsyāmi govinda śreyo me tatra jīvitum
english: Through the weakness of my own judgment, Keśava, I have come up against Bhīṣma; I shall go to the forest, Govinda—better for me to live there.

sanskrit: na tv imān pṛthivīpālān dātuṃ bhīṣmāya mṛtyave kṣapayiṣyati senāṃ me kṛṣṇa bhīṣmo mahāstravit
english: I cannot give over these guardians of the earth to Bhīṣma, to their death; Bhīṣma, knower of great weapons, will surely destroy my army, Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: yathānalaṃ prajvalitaṃ pataṃgāḥ samabhidrutāḥ vināśāyaiva gacchanti tathā me sainiko janaḥ
english: As moths rushing into a blazing fire go only to their destruction, so do the men of my army.

sanskrit: kṣayaṃ nīto 'smi vārṣṇeya rājyahetoḥ parākramī bhrātaraś caiva me vīrāḥ karśitāḥ śarapīḍitāḥ
english: For the sake of a kingdom I, though valiant, have been brought to ruin, scion of the Vṛṣṇis; and my heroic brothers are worn thin, tormented by arrows.

sanskrit: matkṛte bhrātṛsauhārdād rājyād bhraṣṭās tathā sukhāt jīvitaṃ bahu manye 'haṃ jīvitaṃ hy adya durlabham
english: For my sake, out of brotherly love, they have been cast out from kingdom and from ease. I now hold life itself a precious thing, for life today is hard to keep.

sanskrit: jīvitasya hi śeṣeṇa tapas tapsyāmi duścaram na ghātayiṣyāmi raṇe mitrāṇīmāni keśava
english: With what remains of my life I shall practice harsh austerities; I will not have these friends of mine slain in battle, Keśava.

sanskrit: rathān me bahusāhasrān divyair astrair mahābalaḥ ghātayaty aniśaṃ bhīṣmaḥ pravarāṇāṃ prahāriṇām
english: Mighty Bhīṣma ceaselessly destroys my chariot-warriors by the many thousands, the foremost of strikers, with his celestial weapons.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu kṛtvā kṛtaṃ me syād brūhi mādhava māciram madhyastham iva paśyāmi samare savyasācinam
english: What can I do that my purpose may be accomplished? Tell me, Mādhava, without delay. I see Savyasācin standing in the battle as though indifferent.

sanskrit: eko bhīmaḥ paraṃ śaktyā yudhyaty eṣa mahābhujaḥ kevalaṃ bāhuvīryeṇa kṣatradharmam anusmaran
english: Bhīma alone, the mighty-armed, fights with utmost strength, remembering the warrior's duty, by sheer might of arm alone.

sanskrit: gadayā vīraghātinyā yathotsāhaṃ mahāmanāḥ karoty asukaraṃ karma gajāśvarathapattiṣu
english: With his hero-slaying mace, that great-spirited one, to the utmost of his vigor, performs deeds hard to do among elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: nālam eṣa kṣayaṃ kartuṃ parasainyasya māriṣa ārjavenaiva yuddhena vīra varṣaśatair api
english: Yet even he is not able, sir, to bring the enemy host to destruction by fair fighting alone, that hero, not in a hundred years.

sanskrit: eko 'stravit sakhā te 'yaṃ so 'py asmān samupekṣate nirdahyamānān bhīṣmeṇa droṇena ca mahātmanā
english: This friend of yours alone knows the weapons, yet even he disregards us, while we are consumed by Bhīṣma and by the great-souled Droṇa.

sanskrit: divyāny astrāṇi bhīṣmasya droṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ dhakṣyanti kṣatriyān sarvān prayuktāni punaḥ punaḥ
english: The celestial weapons of Bhīṣma and of the great-souled Droṇa, loosed again and again, will burn up all the warriors.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa bhīṣmaḥ susaṃrabdhaḥ sahitaḥ sarvapārthivaiḥ kṣapayiṣyati no nūnaṃ yādṛśo 'sya parākramaḥ
english: Kṛṣṇa, Bhīṣma, fierce in his fury, joined with all the kings, will surely make an end of us—such is his prowess.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ paśya maheṣvāsaṃ yogīṣvara mahāratham yo bhīṣmaṃ śamayet saṃkhye dāvāgniṃ jalado yathā
english: Therefore, O lord of yoga, look out for some great archer, some mighty car-warrior, who might quell Bhīṣma in the fight as a raincloud quells a forest fire.

sanskrit: tava prasādād govinda pāṇḍavā nihatadviṣaḥ svarājyam anusaṃprāptā modiṣyanti sabāndhavāḥ
english: By your grace, Govinda, the Pāṇḍavas, their foes slain, having regained their own kingdom, will rejoice together with their kinsmen."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tataḥ pārtho dhyāyann āste mahāmanāḥ ciram antarmanā bhūtvā śokopahatacetanaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the great-spirited son of Pṛthā sat sunk in thought, long turned inward, his mind overwhelmed by grief.

sanskrit: śokārtaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ jñātvā duḥkhena hatacetasam abravīt tatra govindo harṣayan sarvapāṇḍavān
english: Knowing the Pāṇḍava stricken with grief, his mind broken by sorrow, Govinda then spoke, gladdening all the Pāṇḍavas:

sanskrit: mā śuco bharataśreṣṭha na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi yasya te bhrātaraḥ śūrāḥ sarvalokasya dhanvinaḥ
english: "Grieve not, foremost of the Bharatas; you ought not to grieve, you whose brothers are heroes, archers above all the world.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca priyakṛd rājan sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ virāṭadrupadau vṛddhau dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ
english: And I am here to do you good, O king, and Sātyaki the great car-warrior, and the aged Virāṭa and Drupada, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: tathaiva sabalāḥ sarve rājāno rājasattama tvatprasādaṃ pratīkṣante tvadbhaktāś ca viśāṃ pate
english: And likewise all the kings with their forces, O best of kings, devoted to you, await your favor, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: eṣa te pārṣato nityaṃ hitakāmaḥ priye rataḥ senāpatyam anuprāpto dhṛṣṭadyumno mahābalaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahābāho bhīṣmasya nidhanaṃ kila
english: This son of Pṛṣata, Dhṛṣṭadyumna of mighty strength, ever wishing your good and devoted to your welfare, has been made the commander of your host; and Śikhaṇḍin too, O mighty-armed one, is to be the death of Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tato rājā dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ mahāratham abravīt samitau tasyāṃ vāsudevasya śṛṇvataḥ
english: Hearing this, the king then spoke to Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the great car-warrior, in that assembly, while Vāsudeva listened:

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumna nibodhedaṃ yat tvā vakṣyāmi māriṣa nātikramyaṃ bhavet tac ca vacanaṃ mama bhāṣitam
english: "Dhṛṣṭadyumna, mark well what I shall say to you, sir; this word of mine, once spoken, must not be transgressed.

sanskrit: bhavān senāpatir mahyaṃ vāsudevena saṃmataḥ kārttikeyo yathā nityaṃ devānām abhavat purā tathā tvam api pāṇḍūnāṃ senānīḥ puruṣarṣabha
english: You are my commander-in-chief, approved by Vāsudeva; as Kārttikeya was of old the eternal leader of the gods, so are you the general of the Pāṇḍus, O bull among men.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ puruṣaśārdūla vikramya jahi kauravān ahaṃ ca tvānuyāsyāmi bhīmaḥ kṛṣṇaś ca māriṣa
english: Therefore, O tiger among men, advance boldly and slay the Kauravas; and I will follow after you, and Bhīma, and Kṛṣṇa, sir,

sanskrit: mādrīputrau ca sahitau draupadeyāś ca daṃśitāḥ ye cānye pṛthivīpālāḥ pradhānāḥ puruṣarṣabha
english: and the two sons of Mādrī together, and the sons of Draupadī clad in armor, and those other foremost guardians of the earth, O bull among men."

sanskrit: tata uddharṣayan sarvān dhṛṣṭadyumno 'bhyabhāṣata ahaṃ droṇāntakaḥ pārtha vihitaḥ śaṃbhunā purā
english: Then Dhṛṣṭadyumna, rousing the spirits of all, said: "I, O Pārtha, was ordained of old by Śambhu to be the ender of Droṇa.

sanskrit: raṇe bhīṣmaṃ tathā droṇaṃ kṛpaṃ śalyaṃ jayadratham sarvān adya raṇe dṛptān pratiyotsyāmi pārthiva
english: Bhīṣma in battle, and Droṇa, Kṛpa, Śalya, Jayadratha—all of them, arrogant in war, I shall this day meet in combat, O king."

sanskrit: athotkruṣṭaṃ maheṣvāsaiḥ pāṇḍavair yuddhadurmadaiḥ samudyate pārthivendre pārṣate śatrusūdane
english: Then a shout went up from the great archers, the Pāṇḍavas mad for battle, when that lord of kings, the son of Pṛṣata, the slayer of foes, rose up.

sanskrit: tam abravīt tataḥ pārthaḥ pārṣataṃ pṛtanāpatim vyūhaḥ krauñcāruṇo nāma sarvaśatrunibarhaṇaḥ
english: Then the son of Pṛthā said to the son of Pṛṣata, the commander of the host: "There is a formation called the Krauñca-aruṇa, the crusher of all foes—

sanskrit: yaṃ bṛhaspatir indrāya tadā devāsure 'bravīt taṃ yathāvat prativyūha parānīkavināśanam adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ rājānaḥ paśyantu kurubhiḥ saha
english: the one which Bṛhaspati then declared to Indra in the war of gods and demons. Array it duly, the destroyer of the enemy's ranks; let the kings, together with the Kurus, behold what was never seen before."

sanskrit: tathoktaḥ sa nṛdevena viṣṇur vajrabhṛtā iva prabhāte sarvasainyānām agre cakre dhanaṃjayam
english: Thus addressed by the god among men, as Viṣṇu was by the bearer of the thunderbolt, at daybreak he placed Dhanaṃjaya at the head of all the forces.

sanskrit: ādityapathagaḥ ketus tasyādbhutamanoramaḥ śāsanāt puruhūtasya nirmito viśvakarmaṇā
english: His banner, ranging the path of the sun, wondrous and ravishing to behold, had been fashioned by Viśvakarman at the command of Puruhūta.

sanskrit: indrāyudhasavarṇābhiḥ patākābhir alaṃkṛtaḥ ākāśaga ivākāśe gandharvanagaropamaḥ nṛtyamāna ivābhāti rathacaryāsu māriṣa
english: Adorned with pennants of the hue of Indra's bow, moving through the sky like a thing of the air, resembling a city of the Gandharvas, it seemed to dance, sir, as the chariot wheeled through its courses.

sanskrit: tena ratnavatā pārthaḥ sa ca gāṇḍīvadhanvanā babhūva paramopetaḥ svayaṃbhūr iva bhānunā
english: With that jewel-bright banner and with the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, the son of Pṛthā shone supremely furnished, like the Self-Existent with the sun.

sanskrit: śiro 'bhūd drupado rājā mahatyā senayā vṛtaḥ kuntibhojaś ca caidyaś ca cakṣuṣy āstāṃ janeśvara
english: King Drupada, surrounded by a great army, formed the head; and Kuntibhoja and the Caidya stood at the eyes, O lord of men.

sanskrit: dāśārṇakāḥ prayāgāś ca dāśerakagaṇaiḥ saha anūpagāḥ kirātāś ca grīvāyāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: The Dāśārṇakas and the Prayāgas, together with the bands of the Dāśerakas, the dwellers of the watered lowlands, and the Kirātas, formed the neck, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: paṭaccaraiś ca huṇḍaiś ca rājan pauravakais tathā niṣādaiḥ sahitaś cāpi pṛṣṭham āsīd yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: And with the Paṭaccaras and the Huṇḍas, O king, and the Pauravakas, and together with the Niṣādas, Yudhiṣṭhira held the back.

sanskrit: pakṣau tu bhīmasenaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ draupadeyābhimanyuś ca sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ
english: The two wings were Bhīmasena and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata, the sons of Draupadī and Abhimanyu, and Sātyaki the great car-warrior.

sanskrit: piśācā daradāś caiva puṇḍrāḥ kuṇḍīviṣaiḥ saha maḍakā laḍakāś caiva taṅgaṇāḥ parataṅgaṇāḥ
english: The Piśācas and the Daradas, the Puṇḍras together with the Kuṇḍīviṣas, the Maḍakas and the Laḍakas, the Taṅgaṇas and the Parataṅgaṇas—

sanskrit: bāhlikās tittirāś caiva colāḥ pāṇḍyāś ca bhārata ete janapadā rājan dakṣiṇaṃ pakṣam āśritāḥ
english: the Bāhlīkas and the Tittiras, the Colas and the Pāṇḍyas, O Bhārata—these peoples, O king, took their station on the right wing.

sanskrit: agniveṣyā jagattuṇḍāḥ paladāśāś ca bhārata śabarās tumbupāś caiva vatsāś ca saha nākulaiḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca vāmaṃ pārśvaṃ samāśritāḥ
english: The Agniveṣyas, the Jagattuṇḍas, and the Paladāśas, O Bhārata, the Śabaras and the Tumbupas, and the Vatsas together with the Nākulas—and Nakula and Sahadeva took their station on the left flank.

sanskrit: rathānām ayutaṃ pakṣau śiraś ca niyutaṃ tathā pṛṣṭham arbudam evāsīt sahasrāṇi ca viṃśatiḥ grīvāyāṃ niyutaṃ cāpi sahasrāṇi ca saptatiḥ
english: The two wings held ten thousand chariots, and the head a hundred thousand; the back numbered a hundred million and twenty thousand besides; and at the neck were a hundred thousand and seventy thousand more.

sanskrit: pakṣakoṭiprapakṣeṣu pakṣānteṣu ca vāraṇāḥ jagmuḥ parivṛtā rājaṃś calanta iva parvatāḥ
english: At the wings, their tips, the outer wings, and the wings' ends, the elephants moved hemmed in on every side, O king, like mountains on the march.
